description.narrative: Kyrgyzstan aims to improve legal access, especially for women, youth, and marginalized groups, through inclusive legal processes, strengthened justice institutions, and better alignment of its reforms with national and international standards. The criminal justice system remains crucial for the success of such a change, by upholding the rule of law, protecting human rights, and ensuring public trust; in order to enhance its effectiveness, it is essential to modernize the system through the integration of digital technologies and the strengthening of institutional capacities. This action will thus support the adoption of secure and interoperable digital tools that streamline procedures, improve case management, facilitate evidence handling, and ensure timely communication among key justice actors ¿ including law enforcement, prosecutors, courts, and correctional institutions.The digitalisation of the justice sector has progressed significantly in recent years, reflecting the government's broader efforts to modernise public administration and improve transparency. With the support fo the EU, electronic case management systems has been introduced and a digital court portal allowing citizens and legal professionals to access case information and submit documents online has been developed and isbeing tested. The proposed Action will continue supporting digitisation and digitalisation of the sector, while strengthening cybersecurity and data protection frameworks, thus ensuring the integrity and confidentiality of digital legal records; furthermore it will focus on further digital literacy training for judges, court staff, and citizens in order to help maximise the benefits of new technologies. Furthermore, digitalisation must be accompanied by efforts to build institutional capacity and train personnel to deliver rights-based and people-centered services, ensuring that modernisation efforts do not leave the most disadvantaged behind. At the same time, broadening access to justice requires a focus on inclusivity, fairness and accountability, feeding into a criminal justice system informed by human rights that must be accessible to all individuals, regardless of their socio-economic status, gender, ethnicity, or other potential barriers. Special attention will be given to the needs of vulnerable and marginalised populations, ensuring that legal aid, representation, and court services are available and understandable. Support ot institutional reform efforts will also incorporate gender-sensitive approaches, robust oversight mechanisms, and community engagement strategies to increase public confidence. The proposed action will contribute to the 2021-2027 MIP Priority area 1 (Governance and Digital Transformation), in particular Specific Objective 1 (Promoting Rule of Law and Respect of Human Rights), Specific Objective 2.c (Improvement of the Governance- Improved governance and anti-corruption functions) and Specific objective 3.a and 3.b: (Building of effective, confident and non-discriminatory digitalisation- Strengthened cybersecurity, privacy and data and - Increased access to public electronic services).
